environment.description: Same NestJS microservice deployed on EKS 1.29 with Pod Security Admission (PSA) enforcing 'restricted' profile at namespace level. The pod spec includes an ephemeral emptyDir volume with medium: Memory mounted exclusively at /tmp for the app container (not shared with sidecars which have their own emptyDir mounts). The container runs as non-root UID 10001 with readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and a custom seccomp profile (runtime/default augmented with a deny rule for inotify_add_watch syscall on /tmp paths). Additionally, the node pool runs with a gVisor (runsc) runtime class, which virtualizes the /tmp filesystem per-sandbox and prevents cross-container file descriptor passing. The credential rotation interval is 60 seconds but the Kubernetes-native ExternalSecret operator (using AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation lambda) invalidates any credential at the provider level within 1 second of rotation via a CloudWatch Events trigger, meaning even if a file is read by a local attacker process, the credential is already revoked server-side before it can be used for authentication against the external API.

config.tmp_volume: emptyDir with medium: Memory, per-container (not shared)
config.secret_rotation: ExternalSecret operator + AWS Secrets Manager rotation lambda
config.credential_invalidation: CloudWatch Events trigger revokes at provider within 1s of rotation
config.network_policy: deny-all egress except to external API endpoint via mTLS
config.pod_security_context: runAsNonRoot: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities: drop ALL
